manager.assistant.contextHint: How many recent messages are sent to the model each turn. A lower number keeps small or local models fast and within their context limit; raise it if your model has a large context window. The full chat is always kept on disk.
manager.assistant.group.other: Other languages (reply + speak in that language)
manager.assistant.introHint: The assistant connects to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you choose — pick one below. Free options exist: a local model (Ollama / LM Studio — no key, fully offline), or a free-tier key from OpenRouter or Groq. Or use your own OpenAI key. A key you enter is optional (local servers need none), stored encrypted on this PC, and never included in a pack or export.
manager.assistant.baseUrlHint: The address of an OpenAI-compatible API — it usually ends in /v1. Common ones: OpenRouter https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 · Groq https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 · local Ollama http://localhost:11434/v1 · LM Studio http://localhost:1234/v1. Leave blank to use OpenAI (api.openai.com).
manager.assistant.apiKeyHint: Needed for hosted providers: make a free account at OpenRouter or Groq (or your OpenAI account) and paste the key it gives you (usually starts with sk-). Not needed for a local Ollama/LM Studio — leave it blank. Your key is stored encrypted on this PC and never goes into a pack or export.
manager.assistant.modelIdHint: The exact model name your provider expects — copy it from their models page. Examples: OpenRouter google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free, deepseek/deepseek-chat · Groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile · Ollama/LM Studio the local name like llama3.1 or qwen2.5 · OpenAI gpt-4o-mini.
manager.assistant.voiceHint: Pick the voice that matches your persona's language — a Chinese persona spoken by an English voice comes out garbled. Presets for each language are listed here, and picking a language persona above auto-selects a matching one. To switch between a female and a male voice, pick that language's preset — male voices are available for English, Spanish and French (the “· Male” presets); Chinese, Japanese and Korean are female-only for now. Your own Voice tuning profiles appear here too. “Default voice” is English and does not follow your tuning.
manager.assistant.personaHint: Pick a preset above to fill this in, then tweak it — or write your own and save it below. Replies are read aloud, so keep it plain and short — no lists or emoji. Give it a name and a personality, and say how it should address you (for example, by your name). Another language? Choose a language preset (or write your persona in any language and tell it to reply in that language), then pick a matching voice above — the bank includes English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.

manager.welcome.title: Welcome to Dashboard Engine
manager.welcome.lead: Your desktop is now a live dashboard — it renders straight onto the wallpaper, behind your icons. Here's what you can do from here.
manager.welcome.point1: Browse & switch packs. Eight built-in designs are installed. Pick one in Installed, then “Use on desktop”. Find more under Browse.
manager.welcome.point2: Make it yours. Select a pack and use Customize to recolour it, change the particles, and more — or open it in the editor to rebuild the layout.
manager.welcome.point3: Wire in your life. The Planner puts events on the wallpaper, Launcher pins your apps, and Assistant connects a local or hosted AI you can talk to.
manager.welcome.point4: It stays out of the way. The engine lives in your tray and pauses the animation for full-screen apps. Close this window anytime — the wallpaper keeps running.

create.title: Design your own dashboard pack
create.intro: A pack is a skin, a layout, a persona, and a voice — everything the wallpaper needs to think and speak. Build one in the editor, then share it on Steam Workshop. No account, no code required (though you can add sandboxed code if you want).
create.propsNote: Declare a few of these in your pack so subscribers can adjust it without editing. Values live in their user data, never in your pack.
create.step.0.title: Open a pack in the editor
create.step.0.body: Start from any pack — the built-in packs are the quality floor. Editing a built-in makes your own copy on save; the original is never touched.
create.step.1.title: Arrange the canvas
create.step.1.body: Drag, resize, layer, and duplicate components on a percent-based canvas at your display’s real aspect ratio. What you see is exactly what the desktop renders.
create.step.2.title: Style the skin
create.step.2.body: Set the palette, fonts, textures, ambience particles, and per-component overrides in the inspector.
create.step.3.title: Add Customize knobs
create.step.3.body: Optionally expose a few user-adjustable properties (colours, particles, density) so subscribers can tweak your pack without editing it.
create.step.4.title: Save
create.step.4.body: Your pack lands in your library and on the desktop. Personal data (reminders, pins, notifications, keys) never enters a pack.
create.step.5.title: Publish to Steam Workshop
create.step.5.body: From a pack’s detail panel, publish with a rendered preview + description so others can subscribe.

create.skin.palette.def: void · glass · accent · accentBright · muted · warn · gold — hex colours that drive the whole look.
create.skin.fonts.def: rajdhani · system-sans · system-serif · mono (packs can’t ship font files).
create.skin.ambience.def: none · embers · dust · snow · petals · rain · sparkle, with a density 0.05–1 (reduced-motion safe).
create.skin.wallpaper.def: an image (≤5 MB) or a muted looping video (mp4/webm, ≤30 MB), with fit + focal point.
create.skin.layers.def: stack up to 6 image/video layers with a parallax depth (0–1) + drift — the cursor gives the scene 3-D depth.
create.skin.effects.def: up to 3 WebGL shader effects per layer — ripple, sway, drift-warp, pulse, cursor-ripple, waves, shimmer, shake, spin, scroll, chroma-shift — each scoped by an optional painted mask or region (fail-soft to a static image without WebGL).

editor.insp.note.health: With Live health alerts on, the status line shows your text when all is well and switches to the worst reading (e.g. “CPU 96%”) under high CPU/memory/disk or low battery — amber past 85%, red when critical.
editor.insp.note.notifications: Shows the user’s own live Windows notifications — never saved into the pack. Needs notification access (Windows Settings › Privacy › Notifications).
editor.insp.note.assistant: Clicking this on the desktop opens the AI chat. It runs on a free model by default — pick a different one in the manager under Assistant.
editor.insp.note.launcher: Tiles show the user’s own pins and recents (managed in the manager) — they are never saved into the pack.
editor.insp.note.mixer: Shows each app that's currently using audio, with a live volume slider and mute — the Windows Volume Mixer, on your wallpaper. Only apps playing sound appear; it's Windows-only and desktop-only (a sample shows here in the editor).
editor.insp.note.pomodoro: The timer runs in the background, so it keeps counting — and rings — even while a full-screen app hides the wallpaper. On the desktop you can start, pause, reset, and skip; the editor and library previews show a sample.
pomodoro.notify.focusDone.title: Focus complete
pomodoro.notify.breakDone.title: Break over
editor.insp.note.nowplaying: Shows whatever the user is playing — Spotify, a browser, any player — via the Windows media session, with play/pause/next/prev. Personal data; never saved into the pack. Live only on the desktop.
editor.insp.note.visualizer: Reacts to the system audio on the desktop (any player — Spotify, a browser, a game) via loopback capture. Tip: place a Bloom one full-screen behind your other components for a reactive background ambience. Static preview here; live only on the desktop.
editor.insp.note.module: Runs in a locked-down sandbox — no network, no file access, no control over the engine. It receives the pack theme (--de-* CSS variables + DE.onTheme) and, if enabled, live stats via DE.onData. Full reference in PACKS.md → Module SDK.

editor.insp.note.knobsIntro: Expose a few controls subscribers can tweak without editing the pack. Each knob’s starting value tracks the pack’s current look.
editor.insp.note.knobsLocked: These knobs are set by the pack’s author. Build a pack from scratch, or edit one of your own published packs, to expose your own Customize knobs. (Anyone can still adjust an exposed knob’s value from the library’s Customize panel.)
